title: 4 Things You Need to Be a Great Emcee🎤 1️⃣ Find your “Voice” - Great speakers/emcees have the ability to manipulate thei
caption: 4 Things You Need to Be a Great Emcee🎤 1️⃣ Find your “Voice” - Great speakers/emcees have the ability to manipulate their voice to fit the occasion. Practice in the car, the shower, and the mirror to master your craft.  2️⃣ Master your “Intro and Adlibs”- When you leave the stage, there shouldn’t be a question of “who was he/she” on the mic. Introduce yourself early and often enough that you’re memorable. Learn from others, but make your own. You’ll know you’re on the right page when you hear other people sounding like you😎(I’ve heard a lot of “uh-ohs” and “Wows” lately 😌😅) 3️⃣ Don’t say too little or TOO MUCH - As an emcee, you’re there to facilitate the experience. Talking too much or too little can take away from that, and the crowd will notice.  4️⃣- Identify your “Superpower” - I realized that dancing was something many hosts/emcees couldn’t/wouldnt do, so I used it to help amplify the experience of the event attendees!

title: Disclaimer: It’s worth the read 🤞🏾 This summer, I’ve given a speech, hosted, moderated or emceed 72 events (SEVEN-TWO)…s
caption: Disclaimer: It’s worth the read 🤞🏾 This summer, I’ve given a speech, hosted, moderated or emceed 72 events (SEVEN-TWO)…sometimes multiple in a day, and more often than not, multiple in a week.  High School graduations, career days, curated events, galas, weddings, and even educational pep rallies have trusted me to motivate and/or inspire their audiences to take advantage of each second you have in this lifetime because the only moment you’re promised is the one you’re currently in. 💯 However, transparently, no triumph is absent from trauma…I’ve navigated grief, feelings of inadequacy,disappointment, sleep deprivation, financial lows, and like many of us, have had the “Why me?” conversation with God more times that I can remember.  I started to realize that the answer to my question was, “Because you asked for this.”  -I asked to be relatable to the people I tried to motivate.  -I asked for a platform to make an impact  -I asked for God to reveal to me my real friends and family those other things will come with the territory.. You can’t “Touch” other people without experiencing your own “OUCH”  Last thing I’ll say for y’all who made it to the bottom of this caption (you a real one, cuz I might’ve already scrolled😅) I didn’t get “The Voice” from Durk or from the tv show…it was from an older woman in line at a Publix supermarket the year my grandfather passed away (2015). Her exact words were, “God wants to use you as “the voice” but you need to reach out to your biological father to let go of the anger and hatred you have in your heart. He’s withholding your blessings until you stop running.” Mind you, I’m just trying to buy my pizza rolls. 🍕 ⏩Fast forward to 2021 when I went home to Chicago & met him for the first time, didn’t tell my mom, granny, or sister…I was surprised by my ability to extend grace and forgive. Since that moment, I’ve been able to walk in my purpose. I became The Voice, when I stopped holding myself back and was obedient to what I knew God was telling me.  Make that phone call, send that text & make peace with your pain. You don’t have to forget, but its your job to forgive.  Purpose awaits 🫶🏽 #stayjot#stayjotivatedce

caption: Motivation Monday: Broken to Shine You ever feel like therapy just… breaks you? Like you walked in one way and left feeling like a shattered version of yourself? Yeah… that was me today. But then, I remembered something—a glow stick. A glow stick can’t shine unless it’s broken. You have to snap it, crack it open from the inside, before it lights up the darkness. And isn’t that just like healing? We go through moments that feel unbearable—therapy sessions that dig up wounds we thought were buried, conversations that force us to confront the parts of ourselves we’ve been running from. It’s painful. It’s uncomfortable. It’s messy. But just like that glow stick, once we break open, we start to shine. See, healing isn’t about pretending the cracks don’t exist. It’s about letting the light seep through them. It’s about embracing the breaking because that’s where transformation happens. So if today was hard—if this season of your life feels like a breaking point—remember, that’s not where the story ends. That’s just the part where the light begins. Keep going. Keep growing. And most of all, keep glowing. Happy Motivational Monday. WE got this.✊🏾 Stay Jotivated
